references.text: The Israelite camp at Gilgal is mentioned here as the place where the people encamped after crossing the Jordan, and it became their main base during the conquest of Canaan.
Gilgal was the place where the Israelites celebrated Passover after crossing the Jordan, and it served as their strategic and spiritual center.
The Gibeonites came to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal, confirming that this was the Israelite headquarters during the campaign.
Joshua set out from Gilgal to help the Gibeonites, and verse 43 shows that he returned there after defeating the five Amorite kings.
An earlier return to Gilgal is mentioned here, illustrating the pattern of using Gilgal as a base between military operations.
Gilgal was also the place where Caleb came to Joshua to claim his inheritance, showing the site's continued importance as an administrative center.
